key_insight: The current-driven complete electrode model for electrical impedance tomography can be implemented using standard Robin boundary solves and a small electrode-level system.
engineering_relevance: This provides a portable route to accurate electrode-voltage prediction in standard FEM packages without requiring a dedicated augmented CEM implementation.
method: Solve Robin problems with unit electrode potentials to construct an electrode transadmittance matrix.
Solve the electrode-level system to enforce prescribed total electrode currents.
Prove equivalence to the augmented CEM and formalise discrete energy, equivalence and reference arguments in Lean 4.
evidence_signal: Across five FEM packages using 2D P1 elements, maximum absolute electrode-potential differences were below 5×10⁻¹³ versus EIDORS and errors below 1.1×10⁻¹³ versus an exact rational-arithmetic reference.
watch_item: Equivalence requires an invertible Robin matrix and identical assembled blocks; electrode-current integration and potential-reference handling must be consistent.
paper_title: Implementing the EIT complete electrode model through Robin boundary conditions
